title: Reserve Compass: radial quick-controls for pool scaling & burst policies
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Operators need an immediately accessible, low-friction control surface for Dedicated GPU pools that lets them inspect health, change autoscale parameters, and trigger short-term burst allocations without leaving the pool list or diving into a multi-tab runbook. Current console flows are page-heavy and require multiple clicks to adjust burst windows or preview impact on billing.

Opportunity: Design a compact, contextual control — the Reserve Compass — that surfaces key signals (utilization, latency, error rate), suggests autoscale tuning, and exposes burst presets and one-click overrides. The control should work as an inline expansion for a pool row and as a compact overlay for the pool detail header. It must be keyboard-accessible, mobile-responsive for small tablets, and respectful of RBAC (disable controls when user lacks permission).

Proposed solution summary:
- Visual metaphor: a small radial compass/knob representing current capacity state (green/yellow/red rings) with three radial segments mapping to: min replicas, target concurrency, burst budget.
- Quick actions: preset toggle (Eco / Balanced / Performance), guided slider for transient burst (0-30 min), and a predictive cost preview that updates tokenized estimate in real time.
- Insights strip: a thin sparkline + micro-heatmap for GPU utilization, tail latency p95, and KV cache hit-rate over last 30m. Hover reveals exact values and links to the full telemetry page.
- Safety: confirm modal for burst > 15 minutes and optional owner notification. Draft a disabled state with tooltip when RBAC prevents action.
- Progressive disclosure: advanced controls link to the full Pool Autoscale settings (hysteresis, cooldown, surge policies).

Design goals and constraints:
- Fast: enable common ops tasks in 3 clicks or fewer.
- Safe: prevent accidental long bursts, surface cost impact before apply.
- Observable: every action should be attached to an audit entry and point to a change diff.
- Consistent: reuse Redwood Console tokens and micro-interaction patterns.
- Accessible: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels for radial control, color contrast for ring states.

Success metrics (provisional): reduce time-to-burst by 60% for standard ops flows; fewer post-burst billing surprises (tracked via billing anomalies); increased use of presets by platform teams.
acceptance_criteria: Reserve Compass is implemented as an inline expansion and header overlay prototype in Figma
Prototype includes working interactions for presets, transient burst slider, and cost preview (mocked values)
Design spec documents keyboard and ARIA behaviors for the radial control
Review notes from Eng on feasibility captured and at least one engineering trade-off recorded
RBAC disabled state and confirmation flows defined and documented
Handoff includes assets (SVGs/variants), token mapping, and a short interaction video (30s)
PM signs off on default preset values and notification behavior
comments: 2025-02-13 Ava Chen: Initial concept sketches uploaded to Figma. Focused on reducing page flips for small ops teams.
2025-02-15 Diego Marin: Engineering review done — real-time cost calc will be approximated client-side then confirmed server-side. Need error-state design for failed apply.
2025-02-16 Priya Nair (PM): Prefer a default 'Balanced' preset. Add constraint: burst cannot exceed pool's max GPUs. Flagging requirement for audit log entry on any manual burst.
2025-02-18 Accessibility review (Liam O'Connor): Radial control needs an alternative linear slider + numeric input for screen readers. Added ARIA label draft.
2025-02-19 Design review: Tightened color thresholds for green/yellow/red rings to meet contrast 4.5:1. Added tooltip copy for cost preview explaining approximation.
2025-02-20 Diego Marin: Updated prototype with confirmation modal and 'notify owner' checkbox. Requesting one more pass on microcopy for burst TTL presets.
notes: Implementation hint for Eng: use canvas-based radial with fallback to CSS-based knob for older browsers
Telemetry hook: emit events for preset-click, burst-apply, burst-abort to /console-ops/events
Edge case: if pool is in maintenance mode, compass should show disabled state and link to maintenance notes
